item.description: Wompi , la plataforma de pagos del consorcio colombiano Grupo Cibest, reveló sus estrategias a corto y mediano plazo: amplió el tap to phone a los iPhone, redujo la comisión que cobra por las transferencias hechas con QR y evalúa formar alianzas p ara entrar al mundo del dólar digital y la tokenización. item.title: Novo Nordisk Loses Court Ruling Over Eli Lilly Obesity Drug Ads
item.description: from using advertisements that claim its drugs are more powerful, a setback to Novo as it battles to regain a larger share of the obesity and diabetes drug markets. District Judge Zahid Quraishi ruled Monday that Lilly can continue to make the disputed claims in its ads while Novo proceeds with a lawsuit it filed in July in federal court in Trenton, New Jersey. In one, the drugmaker claims its Zepbound obesity drug is superior to Novo’s Wegovy weight-loss medication.

item.title: Court Rejects Exxon Appeal of $815M Award to Mechanic Over Benzene Exposure
item.description: The Superior Court panel also rejected Exxon’s claims that the award should be invalidated because it was “shockingly excessive and against the weight of the evidence.” Plaintiff Paul Gill was exposed to benzene while working as a mechanic and gas attendant at an ExxonMobil service station in Potter County from 1974 to 1979. has lost its appeal of an $815.5 million compensatory damages judgment that was awarded to a Mobil gas station mechanic who developed leukemia after years of exposure to benzene in its gasoline. In the May 2024 trial in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas jurors heard evidence that ExxonMobil was aware decades ago that there is no safe level of benzene exposure and that Exxon failed to warn Gill of this dangerous and potentially lethal defect in its product, even though “the American Petroleum Institute advised its members, including ExxonMobil, that there was no safe level of benzene exposure in 1948.” Exxon’s defense argued in part that Gill and his medical experts failed to prove that the gasoline caused his cancer.

item.title: Your AI Agents Need A Chief Operating Officer, Too
item.description: At my company, Get Covered , we now run 16 AI agents across more than 3 million rental units. Those numbers make a case for running agents the way you would run staff in a regulated job, with written rules, a defined scope, a manager and a regular review. The best early candidates for agents are tasks where the rules already exist somewhere outside anyone’s head: a statute, a contract clause, an insurance requirement in a vendor agreement.

item.title: Crunchbase Data Shows Q3 Robotics Startup Funding Jumps 185% As US And China Lead Physical AI Push
item.description: Venture funding to robotics startups has soared in 2026, with the bulk of investment going to companies based in China and the U.S., Crunchbase data shows. All told, global venture funding to robotics startups totaled $9.9 billion in Q3, more than double the $4.3 billion invested in Q3 2025, per Crunchbase data 1 . The bulk of robotics funding this year has been in China, with $13.2 billion invested, and the U.S., with $12.1 billion.

item.title: John Seo on 25 years in the catastrophe bond business: Artemis Live video interview
item.description: With specialist catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities (ILS) investment manager Fermat Capital Management celebrating its 25th birthday this year, for our latest Artemis Live video interview we spoke with co-founder and Managing Director of the firm John Seo . Watch the full video interview to learn much more about Fermat Capital Management’s 25 year journey in the catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities market. We discussed Fermat Capital Management’s 25-year history in the catastrophe bond and ILS business, as well as opportunities and challenges for the asset class’ future.

item.title: Fortegra names Guy House as SVP, Treaty Reinsurance
item.description: The Fortegra Group, Inc., a global specialty insurer and part of DB Insurance Co., Ltd., has appointed Guy House as Senior Vice President, Treaty Reinsurance. In his new role at Fortegra, House is tasked with leading the firm’s treaty reinsurance underwriting strategy from the company’s UK office. Fortegra noted that his expertise spans treaty and retrocession reinsurance, direct and facultative (D&F) insurance, exposure management, alongside capital raising and management.

item.title: Client proximity increasingly important in varied EMEA reinsurance market: Swiss Re’s Nikhil da Victoria Lobo
item.description: During the interview, da Victoria Lobo emphasised the importance of staying close to clients and understanding their individual needs in a varied EMEA reinsurance market, explaining that it’s not just one market. Swiss Re expects pricing at the 1 January 2027 renewals across EMEA to vary, emphasising that the region is not a single market and that a deal-by-deal, client-by-client approach is needed to understand individual market idiosyncrasies and match sustainable reinsurance models to clients’ needs. In our latest video interview , Reinsurance News spoke with Nikhil da Victoria Lobo, Head of P&C for Western & Southern Europe and the Middle East & Africa at global reinsurer Swiss Re, ahead of the annual Baden-Baden Reinsurance meeting.

item.title: Oman Re delivers reinsurance revenue increase in 9M’26
item.description: Oman Re, the Sultanate of Oman’s sole reinsurer, has reported an increase in reinsurance revenue for the first nine months of 2026 to OMR 41.1 million (USD 107 million), up from OMR 40.2 million (USD 104.7 million) in the comparable prior year period. Romel Tabaja, Chief Executive Officer, Oman Re, commented, “Oman Re delivered a strong nine-month performance despite regional geopolitical uncertainty and a softening reinsurance market. The reinsurer explained that stronger technical earnings were a key contributor, as the net reinsurance result rose by 134% to OMR 4.2 million (USD 10.9 million), compared with OMR 1.8 million (USD 4.7 million) for 9M’25.

item.title: Register: Risky Future AI Tools for Fraud Detection & Compliance ‘Demo Day’ on October 28
item.description: In partnership with Insurance Journal, Risky Future’s AI Tools for Fraud Detection and Compliance Demo Day will be held on Wednesday, October 28, beginning at 1pm ET. Insurance Journal’s Risky Future series is hosting the “ AI Tools for Fraud Detection and Compliance ” Demo Day, a series of free AI tool demonstrations designed exclusively for insurance carriers, SIU teams, compliance officers, claims leaders, and more. Vendors will highlight pattern recognition, claims fraud detection, premium fraud detection, compliance monitoring and audit automation.

item.title: Anthropic Filing Reveals Concerns Over Data Center Pushback
item.description: “Data center development has prompted public controversy and regulatory scrutiny regarding environmental impact, land and water use,” the company noted in its IPO filing. Anthropic noted in its filing that environmental standards applicable to power generation “continue to evolve, including as a result of changing governmental priorities and shifting public and political views regarding climate change and the appropriate treatment of various power generation sources.” It added that any failure to secure access to adequate electrical power, as well as any legal, regulatory, or other administrative action or change limiting the availability of electricity — or any significant increase in energy or compliance costs — could “adversely affect our cost structure.” Such hurdles would have the potential to “limit our ability to scale our compute infrastructure, develop and deploy our models, and service our customers.” Anthropic also highlighted climate change and environmental concerns more broadly as risk factors, including the potential fallout of extreme weather. had cited force majeure after opposition from environmental nonprofits and regulatory setbacks complicated efforts to secure power for a data center campus in New Mexico.

item.title: FTC, States Sue Dollar General Over Deceptive-Pricing Claims
item.description: The US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states sued Dollar General Corp. Dollar General, which operates more than 21,000 stores, overcharged by millions of dollars in violation of federal and state consumer protection laws, according to a lawsuit filed in Tennessee federal court. “Rather than ensuring its prices at checkout are accurate, for years Dollar General avoided implementing safeguards to prevent continued overcharging, effectively shifting the burden of its own operational shortcomings onto the very communities and consumers who can least afford it,” the complaint alleged.

item.title: AI Adoption Is Outrunning Insurance’s Operational Readiness
item.description: Carriers, brokers and MGAs are racing to layer AI across claims, underwriting, fraud and administrative work, but operational readiness determines how much work those tools can reliably absorb. Insurance leaders should let automation prove itself before changing staffing plans. Insurance headcount grew just 0.81 percent between January 2025 and January 2026, below the 1.42 percent insurers had projected a year earlier, according to The Jacobson Group and Aon’s Q1 2026 U.S.

item.title: Korra Launches Deal Analysis for Non-Catastrophe ILS
item.description: Korra (New York) has launched Deal Analysis, an application for evaluating and pricing casualty, specialty and non-catastrophe property reinsurance and insurance-linked securities transactions. “Deal Analysis brings those pieces together—loss modeling, reinsurance structure, collateral requirements, capital structure, and investor returns—in a transparent modeling environment where reinsurance brokers and capital providers can test assumptions, compare alternative structures, and understand the distribution of potential outcomes,” comments Kyle Safran, Head of Data Science, Korra. Deal Analysis uses AI to extract information and historical loss-triangle data from reinsurance submissions.

item.title: National Life Expands Annuity Portfolio Features
item.description: (Image source: National Life Group website.) National Life Group (Montpelier, Vt./Addison, Texas) has expanded its annuity portfolio with new index crediting options, enhanced lifetime-income features and additional waiver provisions for qualifying health events. “These enhancements are about giving financial professionals and their clients more choices—whether they’re focused on growth potential today, dependable income tomorrow or greater financial flexibility when life doesn’t go according to plan.” National Life has added three index choices to its annuity portfolio: the Bloomberg Mavin 10 Index, Nasdaq-100 Chronos 10% Index and S&P 500 10% Intraday Edge Growth TCA Index. Oran Blumenfeld, VP, Annuity Operations, National Life Group.

item.title: Some Observations About Anthropic’s IPO Filing
item.description: In an S-1 filing today preceding what could be the largest IPO ever , Anthropic laid out extensive new details about its earnings, growth, key stakeholders and the risks it faces going forward. Anthropic also posted a $693 million operating income loss for the first half of 2026, down about two-thirds from last year. Its net loss for this year’s first half was $80 billion, of which about 90% stemmed from what it called a “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFE s.” Each of Anthropic’s seven founders holds between 230,000 and 246,000 shares of Class A stock, per the S-1.

item.title: Buy or Build? Yes.
item.description: A lot of carriers are looking at what AI can do now and asking some version of the same question: Hold on a minute, the world changed, so should we just build everything ourselves? I've spent the last decade building and running Clearcover , an AI-native carrier, and now Dearborn Labs , an AI-native software development firm built specifically for insurance; if anyone was going to tell you to build everything, it would probably be me. But when people ask me whether to buy or build, my answer is...yes.

item.title: Revolut plans private company investment offering
item.description: Working with Carne Group, Revolut plans to let eligible customers invest in private companies through its app, alongside stocks, ETFs and bonds. Revolut has incorporated Revolut Ventures ahead of a planned launch in 2027, according to Rolandas Juteika, who leads wealth and trading at the company. The offering aims to broaden retail access to investments historically reserved for institutional investors.

item.title: Symetra and TIAA launch Mariner Re
item.description: Symetra and TIAA have launched Mariner Re, a Bermuda-domiciled Class E reinsurer backed by a $750 million equity investment from TIAA. Mariner Re will provide capital to support Symetra’s annuity growth through a flow reinsurance arrangement effective October 1, 2026. Symetra Investment Management and TIAA-owned Nuveen will manage the reinsurer’s investments, combining their insurance asset management and institutional investment capabilities.

item.title: L&G launches standalone critical illness coverage
item.description: Legal & General has launched standalone critical illness cover, allowing advisers to recommend the product separately from life insurance or alongside other protection policies. The product provides the same critical illness coverage as L&G’s existing combined life and critical illness products, including children’s cover options. The offering expands L&G’s existing life and critical illness range.

item.title: «Liderar es crear las condiciones para que otros lleguen incluso más lejos que tú»
item.description: Ahí entendí que una de las principales responsabilidades de un líder es rodearse de talento y crear las condiciones para que ese talento pueda crecer y dar lo mejor de sí mismo. Ver crecer a las personas y llegar incluso más lejos que tú es una de las mayores satisfacciones del liderazgo. La primera, y probablemente la que más ha transformado mi forma de entender el liderazgo, fue empezar a construir y liderar equipos diversos y multiculturales.

item.title: Japan Takaichi Orders Cybersecurity Measures as Attacks Grow
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi ordered her cabinet to compile emergency measures by the end of next week to counter a spate of cyberattacks that have rocked Japan in recent weeks. Takaichi also asked her cybersecurity minister, Toshiharu Furukawa, to work closely with allies, like-minded countries and other relevant international organizations to identify the source of the attacks and to form a joint response with the international community. The new framework allows for Japan to deploy “active cyber defense,” meaning that it can take a more proactive stance by identifying and eliminating emerging cybersecurity threats.

item.title: Senator Grassley Adds to Fight for Federal TPLF Disclosure
item.description: Senate’s Judiciary Committee, submitted a letter to the Advisory Committee on Civil Rules to encourage it to amend federal rules of procedure and “increase public disclosure of third party funding in litigation.” Grassley said funders “often prioritize using the courts for monetary return rather than for obtaining justice for the parties involved in the cases.” The practice also has national security implications. Related: Insurance Companies Join Letter to Push TPLF Disclosure in Federal Courts “In addition to providing this data so the practice could be evaluated fairly, required disclosure would help ensure fairness in the courts,” and discourage those with “nefarious intent,” Grassley said.

item.title: Six Flags Will Install Seat Belts on Georgia Roller Coaster After Death
item.description: The chief executive of Six Flags says the company will install seat belts on the Georgia roller coaster from which a rider fell to his death earlier this month. The theme park operator announced the extra safeguard less than two weeks after 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem of Atlanta died after being ejected from his seat on the Goliath coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. patent granted to Bolliger & Mabillard for the restraint system in 2001 says it’s designed to make each rider feel “that he is seated on a flying carpet or that he is at the controls of a kind of flying scooter, while still guaranteeing optimum security.” Following the death in Georgia, non-Six Flags theme parks SeaWorld Orlando in Florida and La Ronde in Montreal, Canada, also temporarily closed one roller coaster apiece that use clamshell restraints.

item.title: Cyber Experts Say AI-discovered Bugs May Trigger More Disruptions
item.description: Advances in artificial intelligence have uncovered a stream of new software vulnerabilities that are almost certain to trigger more disruption along the lines of the outages that percolated across global government websites this week, according to seven cybersecurity professionals who spoke to Reuters. “I think there’s going to be a lot more fire drills for anything that’s internet exposed.” The codebases that run modern programs are sprawling and mistakes, or “bugs,” that open up potential avenues for exploitation often crop up in unexpected places. AI helped drive a doubling of the number of digital flaws discovered year-on-year, according to research due to be published in the coming days by VulnCheck, a Massachusetts-based threat intelligence firm.

item.title: Weather Service Confirms 2 Tornadoes Touched Down in Arizona Last Week
item.description: Two EF-1 tornadoes were reported during storm conditions that rolled through Arizona on October, 21, 2026, according to the National Weather Service forecast office in Flagstaff. EF Scale: The Enhanced Fujita Scale classifies tornadoes into them following categories: EF0…..65 to 85 mph EF1…..86 to 110 mph EF2…..111 to 135 mph EF3…..136 to 165 mph EF4…..166 to 200 mph EF5…..>200 mph A tornado developed south of Heber-Overgaard on Wednesday evening and traveled north across Highway 260 through the town before dissipating near Highway 277, the NWS reported.

item.title: VP Bank stays neutral on cat bonds, notes quiet hurricane season and hedging costs
item.description: Despite the fact premia has reduced in the catastrophe bond market, private bank and asset manager VP Bank AG maintains a neutral weighting on insurance-linked securities noting that the Atlantic hurricane season is currently running its course loss free, although also highlighting the expensive cost of currency hedging. On the positive side, VP Bank notes that the Atlantic hurricane season remains “extremely quiet” having seen over 80% of the season pass before the first hurricane Isaias formed. But additionally and for the first time that we’ve noticed, VP Bank also highlights the expensive cost of currency hedging associated with investments into cat bonds and ILS.

item.title: Sidecars and data centres key opportunity areas for HCMA in 2027: CEO Madea
item.description: As the collateralized reinsurance sidecar market continues to expand, and momentum builds around the data centre build-out, Jarad Madea, Chief Executive Officer of Howden Capital Markets & Advisory (HCMA) told Artemis that those are key areas where HCMA sees future opportunities as the industry begins to head into 2027. Turning back to sidecars, Madea emphasised that expanding these structures across different platforms and geographies will be a central focus for HCMA in 2027. Speaking to Artemis during the reinsurance conference season, Madea discussed how HCMA plans to work more directly with institutional investors looking to deploy capital into casualty sidecars, as well as what he believes are the most exciting opportunities for investors in the reinsurance market today.

item.title: Symetra partners with TIAA to launch sidecar-like life and annuity reinsurer Mariner Re
item.description: Symetra Life Insurance Company, a provider of life, retirement and employee benefit insurance products, has partnered with Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America (TIAA) to launch Mariner Re Ltd., a new Class E licensed reinsurer domiciled in Bermuda, that will initially act as a kind of life and annuity reinsurance sidecar for the company. As we’ve explained in previous articles, structures of this kind act as a type of reinsurance sidecar, fueling additional third-party capital to support life and annuity underwriting business through reinsurance quota share transactions, or flow arrangements, to benefit sponsors like Symetra. Mariner Re supports our ability to grow annuity sales, enhancing our competitive positioning and enabling us to serve more customers.” Dave Dowrich, chief financial officer at TIAA, said: “This transaction allows TIAA to expand and diversify our balance sheet, strengthening our ability to meet the long-term obligations we have to the retirement plan participants who count on us, while deepening our long-standing relationship with Symetra and its parent company, Sumitomo Life.”

item.title: Brown & Brown launches connected intelligence ecosystem to improve insurance decisions
item.description: Brown & Brown has announced the launch of COMPASS, a connected intelligence ecosystem that brings together the company’s data, analytics, specialised knowledge and AI-enabled capabilities to help customers better understand risk and make more informed insurance decisions. Brown & Brown noted that many AI solutions on the market adapt a general-purpose model to a single workflow, whereas COMPASS was built around the data, decisions and experience that drive the insurance business. Steve Hearn, President of Brown & Brown Retail, said, “Insurance organisations have access to more data and technology than ever before, but the industry’s greatest opportunity is to connect those capabilities around the decisions customers and insurance professionals make every day.

item.title: CopperPoint completes acquisition of General Indemnity Group
item.description: CopperPoint Insurance Company, a specialty provider of workers’ compensation and commercial property and casualty insurance solutions, has completed its acquisition of General Indemnity Group (GIG) from Boston Omaha Corporation. In May 2026, CopperPoint announced that it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire GIG. The completion of the acquisition followed the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

item.title: Mariner Re launches with $750m TIAA investment to support Symetra’s annuity growth
item.description: Mariner Re will offer committed growth capital to support Symetra’s annuity business through a flow reinsurance arrangement, effective 1 October 2026. “Mariner Re supports our ability to grow annuity sales, enhancing our competitive positioning and enabling us to serve more customers.” Dave Dowrich, Chief Financial Officer at TIAA, commented, “This transaction allows TIAA to expand and diversify our balance sheet, strengthening our ability to meet the long-term obligations we have to the retirement plan participants who count on us, while deepening our long-standing relationship with Symetra and its parent company, Sumitomo Life.” Nicholas Mocciolo, Chief Investment Officer at Symetra, said, “SIM’s lead role as investment manager reflects our commitment and investment partnership with Mariner Re and Symetra. Symetra Life Insurance Company, a provider of life, retirement and employee benefit insurance products, and Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America (TIAA), a US-based retirement services and financial services provider, have announced the launch of Mariner Re Ltd., a Class E-licensed reinsurer domiciled in Bermuda.

item.title: World Acquires Texas’ Zoom Insurance
item.description: World Insurance Associates announced that it acquired the business of Zoom Insurance of Irving, Texas on July 1, 2026. Zoom offers insurance solutions to individuals, families, businesses, and specialty organizations. Giordano, Halleran & Ciesla provided legal counsel, and Foretrust advised World on the transaction.

item.title: Texas Hill Country Floods Inspire New Law for Emergency Weather Alerts
item.description: The law, called the “Mystic Alerts Act,” comes more than a year after devastating flash flooding in July 2025 killed more than 100 people in the Texas Hill Country, including 27 campers and counselors at Camp Mystic and the camp’s co-executive director. “This law will address this technology shortfall and honor the memory of those lost by ensuring Texans and all Americans can receive wireless emergency alerts on their mobile devices via satellite even when disaster strikes,” Texas Republican Sen. Under a new federal law, National Weather Service warnings of life-threatening flash floods or other emergencies could be sent to cellphones via satellite if cell service goes down.

item.title: Ohio Judge Blocks Lawmakers From Killing Clean Air Law
item.description: The ruling last week from Franklin County Common Pleas Judge Julie Lynch states that lawmakers’ directive to state officials to repeal the air nuisance rule, which was slipped into the state budget as an 11th hour amendment , violated a provision of the state constitution that says legislation can span only a single subject. Since 1974 the rule has been a part of Ohio’s comprehensive plan to comply with the federal Clean Air Act, the bedrock law protecting ambient air in the U.S. A Franklin County judge blocked last week a state law that eliminated Ohioans’ special legal powers to sue polluting neighbors like steel or other industrial plants that spit smoke, ash or other fumes into the sky.

item.title: AmTrust International acquires Wakam to strengthen position in UK and Europe
item.description: AmTrust International, a specialty insurer and subsidiary of AmTrust Financial Services, has completed its acquisition of Wakam, a business-to-business-to-consumer (B2B2C) insurer serving markets across the UK and Europe. AmTrust said Wakam is now fully capitalised and able to immediately write new business and renew policies across all jurisdictions in its portfolio. The transaction expands AmTrust International’s European operations, adding an established presence in France and broadening its existing UK offering.

item.title: Alps expands motor offering on Acturis
item.description: Alps has made its full motor add-on insurance suite available on Acturis , giving brokers access to additional products for individual vehicles and fleets through their existing trading platform. The launch builds on Alps’ Motor Legal Protection range, which joined Acturis in November 2022, and the subsequent addition of its full Let Property add-on suite. The range includes Road Rescue, Guaranteed Hire Vehicle, Motor Excess Protection, GAP, Tools-in-Transit, Key Cover, Parts and Labour cover, and Pothole damage protection.

item.title: Mandl launches as Nirvana exits non-fleet trucking program with SiriusPoint
item.description: The launch follows Nirvana’s decision to exit non-fleet trucking, a segment it wrote in partnership with SiriusPoint . Rushil Goel has launched Mandl , an AI company bringing together three independently run commercial insurance businesses: Nirvana Insurance , Vega Claims and Cooper AI Tech . Nirvana uses driving data and claims outcomes to price commercial fleet risk.

item.title: Amwins’ ARC launches Portfolio Credit program
item.description: Applied Risk Capital ( ARC ), an MGA within Amwins Underwriting, has launched a Portfolio Credit program, expanding its non-payment insurance offering from individual leveraged finance exposures to diversified pools of credit risk. The program covers pools of corporate, sponsor-backed and asset-based credit, including fund-level financing, bank risk transfers and tranched debt structures. It targets banks managing balance sheets and regulatory capital, asset managers financing funds, and insurers seeking rated credit exposure.

item.title: Seguros Azteca: cuando las exclusiones ponen límites a la cobertura antifraude
item.description: Seguros Azteca establece reglas distintas para el fraude en línea y la extorsión, incluso cuando en ambos casos el cliente revela credenciales. Si tú eres sujeto a una extorsión y derivado de esa extorsión lo das, por supuesto que cubre”, aclara a iupana José Landaverde, director de Seguros Azteca. Entregar el número de identificación puede marcar la diferencia entre recibir una indemnización o quedar fuera de la cobertura de un seguro contra el fraude digital.

item.title: Rhode Island Sues Meta Over Alleged Tolerance for Scam Advertising
item.description: Rhode Island sued Meta Platforms in state court last week over the company’s alleged tolerance for widespread scam advertising on its Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp platforms. The suit, filed by Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha in Providence Superior Court, accuses Meta of unlawfully profiting from and participating in the creation of billions of dollars in scam advertising – even as it assured its billions of users that it was working diligently to protect them. Related: Meta to Pay Historic $25 Billion in New Mexico Deception Case The complaint seeks monetary civil penalties for each of Meta’s alleged violations of Rhode Island state law, restitution to consumers, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains and a judicial order requiring the company to address, rather than profit from, scam ads it develops and delivers on its platforms.

item.title: FEMA Launches Online Purchasing for Flood Insurance Policies
item.description: Related: National Flood Insurance Program’s Authority to Expire in December Flood damage is not covered by standard homeowners and renters insurance policies. The Federal Emergency Management Agency said it has launched a new tool for residents to buy flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program. “With this new digital tool, you can get a quote and buy a flood insurance policy in a matter of minutes.” Homeowners can get a free quote after entering information such as address, foundation type, construction type, elevation, and location of HVAC systems.

item.title: Fast-Fashion Group Shein Paying $100 Million to Settle FTC Probe
item.description: Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to settle an investigation by the U.S. The settlement, equivalent to 44% of Shein’s second-quarter profit, is the latest to hit the online fast-fashion retailer facing a regulatory and tax crackdown in Europe and the US that has slammed the brakes on its growth. Consumers filed more than 12,000 complaints about Shein over more than $11 million in purchases between January 2020 and June 2026, according to FTC records reviewed by Reuters.
